slides.texte_overlay:
psychology facts that will
change how you see people

the spotlight effect

people notice your mistakes far less than you think. everyone is busy worrying about their own spotlight, so that awkward thing you said is mostly forgotten already.

the name effect

hearing their own name makes people pay more attention and feel more liked. using someone's name once in a conversation is one of the simplest ways to connect.

the pratfall effect

competent people become more likeable after a small, harmless mistake. being a little imperfect in public makes you feel more human and easier to trust.

the curiosity gap

your brain is wired to want to close gaps in what it knows. spend 5 minutes a day feeding it something new: a fact, a painting, a moment in history. curiosity gets stronger the more you feed it.

the curiosity gap

i used to ignore my curiosity. now i feed it 5 minutes a day with one lesson in the Sophia app: a fact, a painting, a moment in history. it gets stronger the more you feed it.

slides.texte_overlay:
the mirror effect

people tend to like those who subtly mirror their posture and pace. it isn't manipulation when it comes naturally, it's simply how humans show they're on the same page.
